mainTopic: Relying on סימנים and names: the drowned scholars, the sesame deposit, labeled vessels, and the worry about two people with the same name
overview: This amud first finishes the case of the two drowned תלמידי חכמים. Their wives could remarry because the bodies were seen right away and identified by סימנים, so the ruling rested on the marks and not on the women. Next comes a man who deposited sesame with a friend. The friend claims the owner already took it back and that the sesame in his barrel is a different batch. רב חסדא wants to compare this to the drowned scholars, but רבא rejects the comparison. Sesame has no real סימנים, and a matching amount could just be chance. The גמרא then asks whether we worry that a container's contents were emptied and replaced, using a משנה about labeled vessels. It concludes that everyone worries about this, and the argument is only whether the label would have been erased. Finally, a letter reports the death of יצחק ריש גלותא, and אביי and רבא argue whether we must worry that there were two men with the same name. Each brings a proof. The amud ends by asking how אביי answers רבא's proof, and his answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: We relied on the identifying marks, not on the women
steps.stepSummary: The bodies of the two drowned scholars were seen right away, and identifying marks were given. The ruling rested on those marks, not on the women's word.
steps.simpleTranslation: We saw them immediately and they gave identifying marks, because we do not rely on the women, only on the marks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering how the wives could remarry based on testimony from women. The answer is that the real proof was the סימנים, not the women themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two conditions made this work. The bodies were seen right after they came out of the water, before they could change and become hard to recognize. Clear סימנים were also given. Because the proof comes from the marks, the women's usual weakness as witnesses does not matter here.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the precedent רב חסדא will try to use next: when we have סימנים, we trust them and do not worry that the bodies might be different people.

phrases.english: And we saw them immediately,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the two scholars who drowned, seen right when they came up out of the water.

phrases.english: and they stated identifying marks.
For we do not rely on them,
phrases.notes: "Them" here means the women who testified.

phrases.english: but rather on the identifying marks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer that began before this section of the daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the basis of the ruling from the witnesses to the physical marks
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling rests on סימנים seen right away, so women's testimony is not the real basis.

steps.title: The case of the deposited sesame
steps.stepSummary: A man left sesame with a friend. The friend says the owner already took it back and that the sesame in his barrel is a different batch.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man deposited sesame with his friend and asked for it back. The friend said, 'You already took it.' The owner said, 'But it was such-and-such an amount and sitting in a barrel.' The friend answered, 'You took yours. These are other sesame.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new real-life court case about a פקדון (deposit). This case sets up the next move, where רב חסדא compares it to the drowned scholars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner tries to prove the sesame is his by describing it: the amount and the barrel it was in. The friend does not deny there is sesame in the barrel. He only claims it is a different batch. So the whole question is whether the owner's description is strong enough to identify the sesame.

keyTerms.meaning: who deposited (left something in someone's care)

phrases.english: There was a certain man who deposited
sesame with his friend.
He said to him: Give me my sesame.
He said to him: You already took them.
The owner said: But they were such-and-such an amount,
and they are lying in a barrel.
He said to him: You took yours,
and these are other ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּאַפְקֵיד שׁוּמְשְׁמֵי גַּבֵּי חַבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new case that will be measured against the סימנים principle from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. The case presents a deposit dispute in which the owner identifies the sesame only by its amount and location.

steps.title: רב חסדא compares the sesame to the drowned scholars
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא thinks this case matches the drowned scholars. There we did not suspect the bodies were different people, so here too we should not suspect the sesame is a different batch.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא wanted to say: This is just like the two תלמידי חכמים. There we do not say, 'Those men went off somewhere in the world, and these are other people.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא tries to decide the sesame case by comparing it to the drowned scholars. He wants to accept the owner's description, just as the bodies were accepted as the missing husbands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the scholars' case, someone could have argued that the real husbands are alive somewhere and these bodies belong to strangers. We did not take that worry seriously. רב חסדא reasons that the friend's claim, that 'these are different sesame,' is the same kind of far-fetched worry and should be ignored. The word סבר hints that this view will not hold up.

keyTerms.meaning: he thought to say (a view the גמרא is about to reject)
went off somewhere in the world

steps.confusionAlert: סבר רב חסדא למימר means רב חסדא only thought this at first. It is not the final halacha.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda thought to say:
This is the same as the two Torah scholars,
phrases.notes: These are the two scholars who drowned, whose wives were allowed to remarry because of the marks from step 1.

phrases.english: and we do not say:
Those went off somewhere in the world,
and these are other ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְבַר רַב חִסְדָּא לְמֵימַר: הַיְינוּ שְׁנֵי תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to decide the case in step 2 using the precedent in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That the owner's description of the sesame should be accepted, and the claim that these are other sesame ignored
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of the two drowned scholars, where bodies identified by סימנים were not suspected of being other people

steps.title: רבא: sesame has no real identifying marks
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the comparison. The bodies had real סימנים. Sesame has none, and a matching amount could be pure chance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Is it the same? There they gave identifying marks. Here, what identifying marks can sesame have? And when the owner said it was 'such-and-such an amount,' say that the number just happened to match.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down רב חסדא's comparison. The two cases are different because only the scholars' case had real identifying marks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scholars' case worked only because of סימנים, as step 1 stressed. Sesame looks the same from one batch to the next, so it has no סימנים. The amount is not a true mark, because two different batches could easily come out to the same quantity by coincidence. So the owner's claim is not proven.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it comparable? (a challenge to a comparison)

steps.whatToRemember: We rely on סימנים only when the thing truly has distinguishing features. A plain quantity of a common item like sesame is not a סימן, because it could match by coincidence.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches what counts as a real סימן: something that sets the item apart, not a detail that could easily repeat by chance.

phrases.english: Rava said to him: Is it comparable?
There, they stated identifying marks.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא, שׁוּמְשְׁמֵי מַאי סִימָנָא אִית לְהוּ?
phrases.english: Here, what identifying mark does sesame have?
And as for what he said, "They were such-and-such an amount" —
say the amount just happened to match.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב חסדא's comparison in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole comparison between the sesame case and the drowned scholars
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The scholars' case relied on real סימנים. Sesame has none, and a matching amount can be coincidence.

steps.title: Do we really suspect that the contents were swapped?
steps.stepSummary: מר קשישא בר רב חסדא challenges the worry that contents were emptied and replaced. He cites a משנה where a single letter on a vessel is trusted to tell us what is inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר קשישא said to רב אשי: Do we really worry that someone emptied the contents out? We learned in a משנה that if you find a vessel marked with a letter, you trust the letter. ק means קרבן, מ means מעשר, ד means דמוע, ט means טבל, and ת means תרומה. In times of persecution people wrote just a ת instead of the full word תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge begins. מר קשישא asks whether we ever worry that a container's contents were emptied and swapped, the way the friend claimed in the sesame case. He brings a משנה that seems to say we do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, we trust a label without asking whether the original contents were taken out and replaced. That suggests we normally do not suspect a swap. If so, why should we suspect one in the sesame case?

keyTerms.meaning: He emptied them out, moved the contents somewhere else
We are concerned, we take the possibility seriously
A mixture of תרומה and regular produce
Produce whose required gifts have not yet been separated
A time of danger or persecution

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר קַשִּׁישָׁא בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Mar Kashisha son of Rav Chisda said to Rav Ashi:
And are we really concerned that perhaps he emptied them out?
But didn't we learn in a mishna:

phrases.aramaic: מָצָא כְלִי וְכָתוּב עָלָיו קוֹף — קׇרְבָּן,
phrases.english: If one found a vessel with the letter kuf written on it, it is korban;
mem means maaser; dalet means dimua;
tet means tevel; tav means teruma.
For in a time of danger
they would write just tav instead of the word teruma!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the worry about swapped contents that came up in the sesame case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that we suspect a container's contents were emptied and replaced.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה trusts a vessel's label without suspecting that the contents were swapped, so we should not suspect a swap at all.

steps.title: The end of that same משנה does suspect a swap
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers from the סיפא of the same משנה. There רבי יוסי says a barrel labeled 'תרומה' is regular produce, because it may have been emptied and refilled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Don't we worry that someone emptied it? Look at the end of that משנה. רבי יוסי says that even if you find a barrel with the word 'תרומה' written on it, the contents are regular produce. Maybe last year it held תרומה, and then someone emptied it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא pushes back against מר קשישא's proof. He shows that the very same משנה, in its last part, does worry about a swap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוסי, a label does not prove what is in the barrel now, because the תרומה may have been emptied out since then. So the משנה cannot prove that we never suspect a swap. At most, it shows that the first opinion and רבי יוסי argue about this.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the latter part, look at the end of the same source

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
And aren't we concerned that perhaps he emptied them out?
Say the end of that mishna: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ מָצָא חָבִית וְכָתוּב עָלֶיהָ תְּרוּמָה —
phrases.english: Even if one found a barrel with 'teruma' written on it,
its contents are non-sacred,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר: אֶשְׁתָּקַד הֲוָה מָלֵא תְּרוּמָה,
phrases.english: for I say: last year it was full of teruma,
and then he emptied it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא חָיְישִׁינַן שֶׁמָּא פִּינָּן? אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 5 by citing the end of the same משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the labeled-vessel משנה shows we never suspect a swap.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: מר קשישא ignored the סיפא, where רבי יוסי clearly does worry about emptying.

steps.title: Everyone suspects emptying; the question is whether the label would be erased
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that everyone worries about emptying. The two views in the משנה really disagree about whether a person who emptied the vessel would have erased the label.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees that we worry the contents were emptied. They argue about something else. One view says: if he really emptied it, he would have erased the label. The other view says: maybe he forgot to erase it. Or maybe he left the label on purpose, to protect the contents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction between the two parts of the משנה. It moves the argument away from 'do we suspect emptying?' and onto a different question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view trusts the label because a person who emptied the vessel would wipe off a label that is no longer true. רבי יוסי answers that he may have forgotten. Or he may have left a 'תרומה' label so that people would stay away from his regular produce.

keyTerms.meaning: To guard or protect the contents

steps.whatToRemember: Both views agree that contents can be swapped. They only argue about whether a leftover label still tells us anything, or whether the person who emptied it might have forgotten to erase it, or kept it on purpose.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא חָיְישִׁינַן שֶׁמָּא פִּינָּן,
phrases.english: Rather: everyone agrees we are concerned that perhaps he emptied them out,
and here they disagree about this:
One Sage holds: if it were true that he emptied them,
he would surely have wiped off the label.
And the other Sage says: maybe he simply forgot.
Or else, he left it there to protect the contents.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא חָיְישִׁינַן שֶׁמָּא פִּינָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reframes the מחלוקת in the משנה raised in steps 5 and 6: both sides suspect emptying, and they argue only about whether the label would have been erased.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the point of the argument (everyone suspects emptying; the dispute is about erasing the label).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first part of the משנה seemed to ignore the possibility of emptying, while רבי יוסי worried about it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone worries about emptying. The first view assumes the label would have been erased; רבי יוסי says it may have been forgotten or left on purpose.

steps.title: A letter reports that יצחק ריש גלותא died on the road
steps.stepSummary: A new story: יצחק ריש גלותא, the nephew of רב ביבי, died while traveling from קורטבא to אספמיא. A letter was sent with exactly these details.
steps.simpleTranslation: יצחק ריש גלותא, the son of רב ביבי's sister, was traveling from קורטבא to אספמיא and died. They sent a message from there saying: 'יצחק ריש גלותא, son of רב ביבי's sister, was traveling from קורטבא to אספמיא and died.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new case about identifying a man who died far away. This step sets up the facts for the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the information we have is the letter: a name, a title, a family connection, and a route. The question will be whether these details are enough to treat him as certainly dead, so that his wife may remarry.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, the head of the Jewish community in exile
They sent a message from there

phrases.english: Yitzchak the Exilarch,
the son of Rav Beivai's sister,
was traveling from Cortva to Spain, and died.
They sent a message from there:
Yitzchak the Exilarch,
the son of Rav Beivai's sister,
was traveling from Cortva to Spain, and died.

steps.triggerLanguage: יִצְחָק רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא, בַּר אֲחָתֵיהּ דְּרַב בִּיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case about identifying a man who died far away.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A report arrives with a name, title, family connection and travel route of a man who died.

steps.title: Could there be two men named יצחק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether we must worry that another man with the same name and details is the one who died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we worry that there might be two men named יצחק, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the key question about the letter: is it detailed enough to point to only one person?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A name works like a סימן only if it is unique. If another יצחק could fit the same description, the letter does not prove that this particular man died.

phrases.aramaic: מִי חָיְישִׁינַן לִתְרֵי יִצְחָק, אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: Are we concerned about two men named Yitzchak, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי חָיְישִׁינַן לִתְרֵי יִצְחָק, אוֹ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how much the letter from step 8 can be relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a name with its details is a reliable identification, or whether we fear that another person had the same name.

steps.title: אביי worries about two יצחקs; רבא does not
steps.stepSummary: אביי says we do worry that there were two men named יצחק. רבא says we do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We are concerned. רבא said: We are not concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question in opposite ways. Their argument is stated here, without reasons yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, the name and details are not enough, because a second man with the same description is possible. For רבא, these details are specific enough to identify the man.

phrases.english: Abaye said: We are concerned.
Rava said: We are not concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: חָיְישִׁינַן. רָבָא אָמַר: לָא חָיְישִׁינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two opposite answers to the question in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אביי: we suspect there may be two men named יצחק. רבא: we do not suspect this.

steps.title: אביי's proof from the גט found in נהרדעא
steps.stepSummary: אביי proves his view from a גט found in נהרדעא. רבי יהודה נשיאה ruled that the whole city must be checked for another man with the same name.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: How do I know my view? A גט was found in נהרדעא. It said: 'By the קלוניא side of the city, I, אנדרולינאי of נהרדעא, release and send away my wife so-and-so.' The father of שמואל sent the question to רבי יהודה נשיאה, who answered: 'All of נהרדעא must be checked.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a real case to support his view that we must worry about two people with the same name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גט had a name and a city, just like the letter about יצחק ריש גלותא. Still, רבי יהודה נשיאה did not simply rely on it. He ordered all of נהרדעא checked to see if another אנדרולינאי lived there. To אביי, this shows that the worry about a second man with the same name is real.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? (an introduction to bringing a proof)
A גט, a bill of divorce
I release and I send away (standard wording of a גט)
Let it be checked or investigated

phrases.english: Abaye said:
From where do I say it?
For a certain bill of divorce was found in Neharde'a
and it was written: By the kelonya side of the city,
phrases.notes: קלוניא seems to be the name of one side of the city, telling us where the גט was written.

phrases.english: I, Androlinai of Neharde'a,
phrases.notes: אנדרולינאי is the husband's name. The question is whether this is really her husband or another man with the same name.

phrases.english: release and send away
so-and-so, my wife.
And the father of Shmuel sent it
before Rabbi Yehuda Nesia.
And he sent back to him:
All of Neharde'a must be checked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for אביי's position stated in Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's view that we worry about two people with the same name
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה נשיאה's ruling to check all of נהרדעא regarding the found גט

steps.title: רבא rejects the proof: it was only out of respect
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that if the worry were real, the whole world would need checking. So the instruction to check נהרדעא was only to honor the father of שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If that worry were real, he should have said 'Check the whole world!' Instead, he wrote this only out of respect for the father of שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down אביי's proof by showing that the ruling did not really express a true worry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we truly worried about another man with the same name, that man could live anywhere, not just in נהרדעא. Checking only one city makes no sense as a real safeguard. So רבא says רבי יהודה נשיאה did not want to tell the father of שמואל that his question was unnecessary, and he answered in a respectful way.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the ruling was wrong. He is saying the instruction to check נהרדעא was a polite gesture, not a sign of a real halachic worry.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
If it were so,
he should have said 'The whole world must be checked'!
Rather, because of the honor of Shmuel's father
he sent this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof אביי brought in Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only. It does not challenge the facts of the case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Checking only נהרדעא would not address a real worry, so the instruction must have been a matter of respect, not of law.

steps.title: רבא's proof from loan documents in מחוזא
steps.stepSummary: רבא proves his view: רבא בר אבוה collected money using documents with names that were very common in מחוזא, and he did not worry about other people with those names.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: How do I know my view? Two loan documents came out in מחוזא. They had the names חבי בר ננאי and ננאי בר חבי, and רבא בר אבוה collected money with them. Yet those names were very common in מחוזא.
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבא brings his own proof that we do not worry about another person with the same name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many men in מחוזא had these same names, so it would have been easy to suspect the documents belonged to someone else. Still, רבא בר אבוה let them be collected without any check. To רבא, this shows that a matching name and details are trusted.

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do I say it?
For there were two documents that came out in Mechoza
and written in them was:

phrases.aramaic: חָבֵי בַּר נַנַּאי וְנַנַּאי בַּר חָבֵי,
phrases.english: Chavai bar Nanai and Nanai bar Chavai,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַגְבִּי בְּהוּ רָבָא בַּר אֲבוּהּ זוּזֵי.
phrases.english: and Rava bar Avuh collected money with them.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא חָבֵי בַּר נַנַּאי וְנַנַּאי בַּר חָבֵי
phrases.english: But Chavai bar Nanai and Nanai bar Chavai
are very common in Mechoza.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting אביי's proof, רבא brings his own support.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that we do not worry about two people with the same name
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא בר אבוה collected loan documents bearing common names in מחוזא

steps.title: How does אביי deal with רבא's proof?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what אביי would say about the documents from מחוזא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי, how would he answer this?
steps.whatsHappening: This short line sets up the next move. The גמרא asks how אביי would explain away רבא's proof, and his answer is coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's proof seems strong, since common names were trusted in a money case. The גמרא now turns to אביי to see how he would answer it. This repeats the pattern of Step 12, where רבא answered אביי's proof.

phrases.english: And Abaye?
phrases.notes: Short for: how would אביי answer this proof against his view?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבא's proof from Step 13 into a challenge that אביי must answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How אביי would answer רבא's proof from the loan documents in מחוזא
